title: Deviled Eggs
description: The classic: a smooth, tangy yolk filling of mayonnaise, yellow mustard and a splash of white vinegar, dusted with paprika. The whole trick is mashing the yolks fine before anything wet goes in.

steps.heading: Hard-Boil
steps.text: Lay the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Bring to a full boil over high heat, then cover, take the pan off the heat and leave for 12 minutes.

steps.heading: Chill & Peel
steps.text: Move the eggs straight into a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes. Crack them all over and peel under running water, starting from the wide end where the air pocket is.

steps.heading: Halve
steps.text: Slice each egg in half lengthwise with a sharp knife, wiping the blade between eggs. Pop the yolks into a bowl and set the whites on a platter, hollow side up.

steps.heading: Make the Filling
steps.text: Mash the yolks with a fork until they are fine, even crumbs with no lumps left. Only then add the mayonnaise, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper, and stir until completely smooth. Taste and adjust.

steps.heading: Fill
steps.text: Spoon the filling into the whites, or pipe it from a zip-top bag with one corner snipped off. Dust with paprika just before serving.

notes: Eggs a week or so old peel far more cleanly than very fresh ones. Make-ahead: keep the whites and filling separately, covered, in the fridge for up to 2 days and fill shortly before serving so the whites don't go soggy.
